items.text: A bar use requires a Conditional Use Authorization hearing and must transfer an existing bar license from within the Mission Alcohol SUD; the only modern bar CUA on this block was withdrawn, and the high license density will trigger ABC undue-concentration review.
Planning Code §762 and §249.60 classify Bar as a conditional use in NCT-VALENCIA and require Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60) provides that a new or relocated Bar is conditional under the underlying zoning but must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD.
An active ABC Type 41 (On-Sale Beer & Wine – Eating Place) license was issued to Sarita's Grill & Beer at 995 Valencia St on 2023-11-03, establishing restaurant use, not bar use.

A Conditional Use Authorization for a bar within a full-service restaurant was filed for 970–974 Valencia St (66 m away, same NCT-VALENCIA zoning) on 2010-08-12 and withdrawn on 2011-01-14; it is the only modern bar-use CUA filed on this block of Valencia.

Planning approved ABC license continuations on Valencia Street but stated in 2008 that approval of a Type 41 eating-place license does not establish a new bar use, distinguishing restaurant from bar under the Planning Code.

Bar use is conditional in NCT-VALENCIA and the Mission Alcohol SUD (§249.60) requires the applicant to transfer a Type 42 or 48 license from another bar within the SUD; no record shows such a license is available, and the only bar CUA on this block was withdrawn in 2011.

The density statistics show 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft and 51 within 1,000 ft, with an undue_concentration_flag set to true, indicating ABC will likely require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) finding from the city.

ABC Type 42 (beer-and-wine bar) licenses are non-quota so new licenses are issued directly by ABC, but nearly every city treats a Type 42 as a bar use requiring conditional use or police/planning review before ABC will issue.

An active Type 41 eating-place license (Sarita's Grill & Beer, issued 2023-11-03) exists at 995 Valencia; transferring it to a Type 42 bar license will require surrender of the Type 41 and Planning approval of the change of use to bar.

ABC's undue-concentration review in high-density tracts adds 1–3 months to the timeline and requires a PCN letter from the Planning Commission or Board of Supervisors; start that process in parallel with the CUA filing.

A Type 42 bar license is non-quota so ABC will issue it, but 9 active on-sale licenses within 500 ft trigger undue-concentration review and ABC will require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the City before issuance.
A Place of Entertainment permit is required when entertainment is a primary use or live music and amplified sound run until 2 a.m., per Planning Code §762 and Police Code §1060.
An active Place of Entertainment permit (no. 1243) is on file for Amados at 998 Valencia St, 31 m from the subject site, showing POE permits are approved on this block.

Planning approved an Entertainment Commission POE referral in 2014 for 998 Valencia, authorizing live entertainment accessory to retail use and limited to ⅓ of gross floor area, showing the Commission grants POE permits with area caps.

A POE permit for a restaurant and nighttime entertainment use at 2512 Mission (152 m, NCT-MISSION) was approved in 2020, indicating the Commission approves POE permits for food-and-drink concepts with entertainment in Mission NCT districts.

Live entertainment and amplified sound after midnight require a Place of Entertainment permit; the nearest POE (Amados, 31 m away) shows approval is feasible, but the Commission will hold a public hearing and may impose sound-level and hours conditions.
The FY2026–27 fee schedule sets the Permit to Operate application fee at $470 (includes initial inspection) and the annual license fee for restaurants and bars at $0 for 2026–28.
DPH approved a restaurant health permit referral for 995 Valencia St on 2021-01-20 as a continuation of restaurant use per §102 and §762.
Site history shows continuous restaurant use at 995 Valencia since at least 1999, with DPH and ABC approvals for full-service restaurant operations in 1999, 2001, 2002, 2010, and 2020.

A limited-cooking food facility serving small plates is principally permitted and requires DPH plan check, a certified food manager, and a final pre-opening inspection; site history shows continuous restaurant use since 1999.
A building permit with a change of use (restaurant → bar) is routed to Planning for zoning review and neighborhood notification per Planning Code §312 where required.

Kitchen build-outs, hoods, restrooms, ADA upgrades, and any change of occupancy need a DBI permit with plans stamped by an architect; full plan review with Planning, Fire, Public Health, and PUC routing takes 2–4 months.
Any new or remodeled food facility needs DPH plan-check approval of finishes, equipment, and menu; FY2026–27 fees run $828–$2,207 depending on scope.

Tenant improvements for a limited kitchen, bar build-out, and ADA upgrades will require a building permit with DBI, DPH, and Planning routing; a change of use from restaurant to bar will trigger Planning Code §312 neighborhood notification.

Expected condition: Hours of operation limited to 6 a.m.–2 a.m. (state law maximum for on-sale alcohol); no operation between 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. without an Extended Hours Premises permit. Basis: Planning Code §762 shows hours of operation 6 a.m.–2 a.m. are principally permitted and 2 a.m.–6 a.m. are conditional. State law prohibits alcohol sales after 2 a.m.

Expected condition: Live entertainment area capped at ⅓ of gross floor area, with posted occupancy limits and compliance with Fire Department Place of Assembly permit requirements if occupant load reaches 50. Basis: The 2014 POE approval at 998 Valencia limited entertainment to ⅓ of floor area per Police Code §1060(r). At 40 seats this concept is likely below the 50-person Place of Assembly threshold.

Expected condition: Sound-level limits measured at the property line and at upstairs residential units, noise monitoring, and a written good-neighbor policy addressing sound complaints and late-night patron management. Basis: The Mission Alcohol SUD imposes good-neighbor operating conditions per §202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits. POE permits for entertainment venues commonly include sound-level conditions.

Expected condition: ABC Type 42 license limited to beer and wine only, with no minors allowed on the premises under state law, and compliance with ABC RBS training for all alcohol servers and managers within 60 days of hire. Basis: The Type 42 catalog entry states no minors are allowed and ABC RBS training is mandatory under AB 1221 for every alcohol server and manager within 60 days of hire.

Expected condition: No expansion of the bar area or change in mode of operation without a new Conditional Use Authorization, consistent with Planning's policy for existing alcohol-serving uses in the Mission Alcohol SUD. Basis: The 2006 ABC referral approval at 1101 Valencia prohibited expansion of the bar square footage or change in character of operation, reflecting the Mission Alcohol SUD policy that existing bars cannot expand.

Expected condition: Compliance with the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, including a community liaison, posted complaint hotline, and annual reporting on noise complaints and security incidents. Basis: The 2026 Project Profile Lite for the nightclub at 2500 Mission states the use is subject to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, indicating this is a standard condition for POE permits.

Filing step: File for a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to discuss the bar CUA, Mission Alcohol SUD license-transfer requirement, and likely conditions. What to say: Request a pre-application meeting under Planning Code §312. Explain that the concept is a 40-seat beer-and-wine bar with limited kitchen and live music until midnight, and that you are seeking to transfer a Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD per §249.60. Ask what conditions (hours, sound, security, good-neighbor policy) the Commission will require and whether the current restaurant use simplifies the hearing.

Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for bar use, along with the required neighborhood notification and environmental review. What to say: Frame the project as a conversion of an existing restaurant to a beer-and-wine bar with occasional live music, emphasizing the transfer of an in-district bar license per §249.60 and the limited scale (40 seats, beer and wine only, no dancing). Commit to a good-neighbor policy, sound monitoring, posted complaint hotline, and hours of operation ending at 1 a.m. or earlier if the Commission requests. Attach an acoustic study showing the space can meet residential sound limits, a security plan, and letters of support from the neighborhood association and nearby businesses.

Filing step: In parallel with the CUA, file for a Place of Entertainment permit intake meeting with the Entertainment Commission. What to say: Email the Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility and request an intake meeting. Explain that live music will be occasional (1–2 nights per week), end by midnight, and occupy no more than ⅓ of the floor area. Commit to the Good Neighbor Policy, sound-level monitoring, and an annual report on complaints. Attach the same acoustic study and security plan submitted with the CUA, and state that the POE application will be complete once the CUA is approved.

Filing step: Once the CUA is approved, file the Place of Entertainment permit application with the Entertainment Commission, including the $2,708 fee, posted notice, and Police/Planning referrals. What to say: Submit the POE application online with proof of the approved CUA, the lease, the acoustic study, the security plan, and the good-neighbor policy. Post the yellow notice at the premises for 30 days and notify neighbors within 300 ft. Coordinate with SFPD and Planning for their referral sign-offs before the Commission hearing.

Filing step: After CUA approval, apply to ABC for the Type 42 license, including the city's Public Convenience or Necessity finding if required by the undue-concentration review. What to say: Submit the ABC Type 42 application with proof of the approved CUA, the lease, the seller's permit, the entity registration, and workers' comp insurance. Include the Planning Commission's PCN finding letter if ABC requests it due to high license density. Post the 30-day public notice at the premises and comply with ABC's transfer and investigation timeline.

Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements, including DPH plan check, Fire, and Planning routing. What to say: Submit stamped architectural plans showing the limited kitchen, bar layout, ADA upgrades, restrooms, and any soundproofing or HVAC work. Route the application to DPH for health plan check, Fire for hood and suppression review, and Planning for zoning sign-off. Indicate that the CUA and POE permit are approved and attach copies. Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at 80% completion and the final inspection before opening.

Filing step: After the final DBI and DPH inspections, apply for the Health Permit to Operate and obtain ASCAP, BMI, and RBS certifications for staff in the final two weeks before opening. What to say: Submit the Health Permit application online with the Business Account Number, the certified food manager certificate, and proof that the building permit final was issued. Schedule the DPH final inspection. Enroll staff in ABC RBS training and obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before the first day of music programming.

Entitlement path: CUA for bar use + Mission Alcohol SUD license transfer + Place of Entertainment permit + ABC Type 42 with PCN finding + building permit and health permit. Estimated time: 240 to 480 days. Estimated government cost: $9,300 to $26,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog) plus the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, filed after CUA approval). ABC Type 42 processing (60–150 days) runs in parallel with the POE permit once the CUA is approved, but undue-concentration review will add 1–3 months and require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from Planning. Building permit plan review (14–120 days) can start after the CUA is approved. Total timeline: 8–16 months from CUA filing to opening. Government fees include CUA application ~$3,100, POE permit $2,708, ABC Type 42 $1,000–$1,600, Health plan check $828–$2,207, Health Permit $470, Building permit $800–$15,000 (depending on construction cost), plus state/federal registrations ~$300. The largest uncertainty is whether a Type 42 or 48 license is available for transfer from within the Mission Alcohol SUD; if none exists, the concept cannot be approved as a bar and must be re-framed as a restaurant with accessory entertainment. The second risk is the CUA hearing: the only bar CUA filed on this block was withdrawn, and the records show no new bar approvals in the modern SUD era. Plan for 10–12 months and $12,000–$18,000 in fees if a transferable license is secured and the CUA is approved; 16+ months if the undue-concentration PCN process or a CUA appeal adds delay.
